title: Ide
description: The Ide dialect — one Igbo dialect, not a language of its own. Its voice is Idemmili; its base is the speech of Ọmambala and Idemmili with Onicha, Nkpor and their neighbours; and its borrowed layer is the non-Igbo words it took from Igala, Fulfulde, Kanuri, Tiv, Idoma and Ekoi.

SEVEN PARTS

The contents

Every page of the record, in the order it belongs.

Part I

The dialect

What Ide is, how it sounds, and where its words came from.

  • The Ide dialect — one Igbo dialect, a fusion of Central and Northern Anambra speech
  • How it is spoken — the sound rules, and every word with its recording
  • The dialect readings — every concept with the variety it was read from
  • The borrowed layer — the non-Igbo words, by source language

Part II

The people

The house, the grades of life, what is held, what is made, what is eaten.

  • Culture — the whole of it, part by part
  • The house — the two councils, the grades, the temple, the king
  • The age grades — from Omuazi at birth to the title
  • What is made — the instruments, the dress, the buildings
  • The food — the dishes and the words the cooking is named with
  • What is held — water, fire, the earth, and the forms named

Part III

The polity

Who holds authority, and in what proportion.

  • Leadership — the Ikala, the Iyi, the councils, and the 35 percent rule
  • Polity and title — the titles and the offices
  • The seven uniku — the seven clans, and ebo for a subclan
  • Festival and rite — the feasts, the rites, and egwu ede

Part IV

The dictionary

The vocabulary of record, A to Z and by topic.

  • Dictionary — 7,173 entries, searchable
  • Words by topic — every section, and the alphabet
  • The recordings — 311 words carry their own recording

Part V

The written record

The documents themselves, readable in full.

  • Library — the written record and the register
  • The Ide kingdom — the civil architecture in full
  • The Ide subgroup of Igbo — where the Ide sit among the Igbo
  • Ide tribe names — the names and what each one means
  • Ide burial tradition — the canon of Ana burial
  • Ndose — the sacred spaces, and how they are built

Part VI

The religion

Odiana, read in the Ide dialect.

  • Odiana — the religion of the Igbo, in Ide
  • Obibi Nso — the scripture itself, in full
  • Doctrine — what is taught
  • The home — the dwelling, arranged and kept

Part VII

The objects

The material culture, in photographs.

  • Gallery — the instruments, the dress and the architecture
  • The clothing — Uwe Ibobo and Uwe Ogodo, with the garment photographs
  • The family register — 650 names
